newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank sees recovery, cuts rates again.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank sees recovery, cuts rates again.

text.p: Sweden's Riksbank Tuesday signalled its growing faith in the country's nascent economic recovery in an upbeat inflation report that coincided with the 20th cut this year in the bank's key interest rate.
In its latest quarterly report on economic developments and monetary policy, the central bank said inflation in Sweden -- now running at just 0.6 percent -- had been held firmly in check.
"The prospect of inflation during 1997, as well as in the first half of 1998, being in line with the 2 percent inflation target is good," the bank said.
In fact, inflation was lower than envisaged in the bank's last report, which was published in June.

"This is primarily because the transitory effects of falling interest rates and import prices have been greater than expected," the Riksbank said, adding that economic developments had otherwise been in line with its previous assessments.
With the threat of inflation firmly banished, the central bank said the way was clear for further cuts in its key interest rate, the repo rate.

This was underlined just half an hour after the publication of the inflation report, when the bank trimmed the repo rate, which is its main monetary policy tool, by a further 10 basis points to 5.05 percent in what was the 20th such move this year.

The repo rate has fallen by almost four percentage points from 8.91 percent in January, while the Swedish crown has steadily appreciated against the German mark and the rate of inflation has continually fallen.
The main cloud on the Swedish economic horizon has been growth, or lack of it, but the Riksbank said it was slightly more optimistic in this respect too.
"The economic slowdown toward the end of 1995 was brief, and there has been an upturn during 1996," the bank said.
"A total growth rate of 3 to 4 percent for 1996 and 1997 combined is still considered most probable, although today the emphasis is in the upper half of this interval."
